new_statements.translation: § 6. — The tonic accent always falls on the penultimate. E.g. múnu 'man'; usíku 'night'; bánde 'outside', etc. Monosyllables are either enclitic or proclitic. E.g. bá ndo 'near the hut'; mu múmbu 'in the earth'; mand'áe 'his/her sister'; muli'ánge 'my chief', etc. A few monosyllabic verbs are nevertheless accented, but the case is less frequent than in Subiya.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress ('accent tonique') is fixed on the penultimate syllable of the word. Monosyllabic words do not carry their own accent but attach as proclitics or enclitics to a neighbouring word, so the penultimate is computed over the clitic group (bá ndo, mu múmbu, mand'áe, muli'ánge); a few monosyllabic verbs are exceptionally accented. Jacottet also treats double vowels as two syllables (1901: 495 n. 2), so the penult is counted by vowel morae/syllables, not by the long-vowel sequence.
new_statements.exceptions: Monosyllables are unaccented clitics (proclitic or enclitic); 'quelques verbes monosyllabiques' are nevertheless accented, less often than in Subiya. No other exceptions given.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, stated as an absolute rule ('toujours'); examples are single nouns and clitic-plus-noun groups (locative/possessive phrases), so the domain is the phonological word including clitics. Jacottet treats 'accent tonique' as stress in 1890s missionary usage; nothing is said about tone, and the description dates from 1895 fieldwork with A-Louyi speakers (informant Kaboukou) in Basutoland, not in situ. No modern (post-1970) source on Luyi prosody could be opened.
new_statements.identity_note: Jacottet's 'Louyi' (Si-Louyi, spoken by the A-Louyi/A-Louyana, the ruling Barotse/Rotsi tribe of the Upper Zambezi) is Luyana proper = Glottolog luya1241 (Luyi), ISO lyn, distinct from Lozi (Sotho-based, lozi1239). The grammar was written from 1895 dictation by the Luyi speaker Kaboukou at the Paris Mission in Basutoland, later checked with two more A-Louyi speakers (1900); it represents the language of the 'A-Louyi proprement dits' (Jacottet 1896: intro p. ix-x), not the Kwangwa/Mbowe/Kwandi/Mashi dialects. PHOIBLE's 'Louyi' inventory PH 890 and the Rosetta Project lyn files are built from this same sketch.
